page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, operating on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, this instance provides dedicated CPU allocation. The processor configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or a bundled GPU.

Performance benchmarks place the n4-standard-8 in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, consistently register in the middle 50% of tested servers. Memory read bandwidth reaches 530.44 GB/sec for small cached blocks and drops to 61.33 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, while Passmark memory scores fall into the bottom 25%. The instance demonstrates moderate capabilities in text processing, image processing, and software compilation. However, it exhibits performance limitations in multi-threaded decompression and large-model LLM text generation, where the 7B model text generation speed drops to a poor 6.31 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-8 offers a balanced resource profile suitable for standard enterprise workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Its dedicated CPU allocation and AMX instruction support make it a viable option for lightweight machine learning inference, static web serving, database operations, and general-purpose application hosting. It is best suited for workloads that require a steady 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but do not demand high-throughput local storage or intensive multi-threaded memory performance.
